changes.title: Drop the changeme LXC password default from git-managed defaults

context:
Goal: remove the hardcoded `password: changeme` LXC default so every unmodified clone provisions containers with SSH-key access only and no shared root password.

Single source of the defect: `ansible/vars/homelabinfra-defaults.yml:12` sets `homelabinfra_defaults.proxmox.lxc.password: changeme`. Because config layer 1 (git-managed defaults) merges into `homelabinfra_config` via `combine(recursive=True)` and no user config overrides it, every container created by a fresh clone receives a known root password. This violates specs/secrets-handling.md ("No hardcoded credential defaults that could survive to production (e.g. `password: changeme` in git-managed defaults). Generate, prompt, or fail.").

Why key-only access is safe (approach settled in Analyze — drop the key entirely, no generated/prompted replacement): `ansible/tasks/proxmox/lxc-create.yml` asserts `homelabinfra_config.ansible.ssh_public_key is defined` (line 7) and passes it as `pubkey` to the module (line 28). `ssh_public_key` is a required key in `config.example/proxmox.yml` (`ansible.ssh_public_key`), so every deploy already installs the user's public key on the guest. Root SSH access therefore does not depend on the password. The `community.proxmox.proxmox` 2.0.0 argument spec declares `password` as optional (no `required=True`, absent from every `required_if`), so a container is created successfully with a `pubkey` and no `password` (confirmed in Analyze).

Why no allowlist change is needed: `lxc-create.yml` builds module args by intersecting `homelabinfra_instance.lxc` keys with the `lxc_module_keys` allowlist (lines 74-119, meta slice 003). `password` is already listed at line 101. The instance dict is assembled from `homelabinfra_config.proxmox.lxc` (line 29); once the default is gone and no user supplies one, `password` is simply absent from the intersection and never reaches the module. The allowlist keeps `password` so a user who deliberately sets `proxmox.lxc.password` in their own `config/apps/<instance>.yml` still works.

Why the key must be removed, not blanked: per specs/config-layering.md, an empty-string value in a git-managed layer still overrides a real value supplied by a lower layer under `combine`. Removing the line entirely lets a user-supplied password fall through cleanly and leaves no literal in git.

No-null-subtree check: after deleting line 12 the `proxmox.lxc` subtree still holds `disk_volume`, `cores`, `description`, `features`, `memory`, `onboot`, `tags` — it is not reduced to a null/empty subtree, so no `{}` placeholder or assert change is required.

Blast radius: exactly one line in one git-managed defaults file. No task file, example file (`config.example/proxmox.yml` and `config.example/apps/*` carry no LXC password), `CONTRACT.md`, or app-default references the LXC password. `configure-pbs.yml:15` mentions a PBS admin password in an unrelated comment; `vm-create.yml:129` handles `cipassword` for VMs — both are out of scope.

Out of scope (do not touch): `lxc-create.yml:145-153` writes `homelabinfra_instance.lxc | to_nice_json` (which still includes `api_token_secret`) to `/root/home` on the guest — a separate pre-existing secrets-handling concern not covered by this specimen's goal.

matter.content:
### Goal
Eliminate the `password: changeme` default for LXC containers in git-managed defaults — every
container created by a user who didn't override it currently gets a known root password.

### Context
`ansible/vars/homelabinfra-defaults.yml:12` ships `proxmox.lxc.password: changeme` to every
clone of this repo. Containers are also provisioned with the user's SSH public key
(`pubkey`, `tasks/proxmox/lxc-create.yml:28`), so password auth is not needed for the platform to
function. Per specs/secrets-handling.md, no hardcoded credential defaults.

Options for the groomer to weigh: (a) drop the key entirely and let the module create the
container without a password (key-only access — verify the `community.proxmox.proxmox` module
accepts absence), (b) generate a random per-container password at create time with
`lookup('password', ...)` — but then it must be stored somewhere useful (Vaultwarden isn't up at
LXC-create time during bootstrap; writing it anywhere else violates the secrets spec), or
(c) require the user to set it explicitly, assert with a friendly message when both password and
pubkey are absent. The philosophy "defaults cover 80%" favors (a) if the module allows it.
Related: meta slice 003's module-arg allowlist decides which keys reach the module at all —
coordinate if both are in flight.

### Acceptance criteria
- `vars/homelabinfra-defaults.yml` contains no literal password value.
- A default deploy still yields root SSH access via the configured public key.
- If a password path is kept, it is user-supplied or generated-and-stored per
  specs/secrets-handling.md — never a shared literal in git.
- The `lint` gate from `.claude/build.yml` passes on the touched files.

prerequisites: ansible/vars/homelabinfra-defaults.yml line 12 sets homelabinfra_defaults.proxmox.lxc.password: changeme, shipping a known root password to every unmodified clone.

ansible/tasks/proxmox/lxc-create.yml passes pubkey from homelabinfra_config.ansible.ssh_public_key (line 28) and asserts ssh_public_key is defined (line 7), so root SSH access does not depend on the password.

The community.proxmox.proxmox module declares password as optional (password=dict(no_log=True), no required=True, absent from every required_if), so a container is created successfully with a pubkey and no password.

The LXC module-arg allowlist in lxc-create.yml (meta slice 003) already lists password among lxc_module_keys and builds args by key intersection, so removing the default drops password from the module call with no allowlist change.

rounds.abstract: Removed the hardcoded `password: changeme` LXC default from ansible/vars/homelabinfra-defaults.yml so default LXC containers are created with SSH-key access only and no shared root password.
rounds.details: Deleted the single line `      password: changeme` (was line 12) nested under `homelabinfra_defaults.proxmox.lxc`. The `proxmox.lxc` subtree now flows directly from `disk_volume` (storage/size children intact) to `cores: 1` and retains all remaining keys: disk_volume, cores, description, features, memory, onboot, tags — no null/empty subtree introduced (AC1, AC2). No other line, file, example, or task was touched; the `lxc_module_keys` allowlist in tasks/proxmox/lxc-create.yml still lists `password`, so a user who explicitly sets proxmox.lxc.password in their own config/apps/<instance>.yml still has it forwarded to the module (AC4). With the default gone and no user override, `homelabinfra_instance.lxc` carries no `password` key, the allowlist intersection omits it, and the module is invoked with the required `pubkey` (ssh_public_key, asserted at lxc-create.yml:7) and no `password`, yielding key-only root SSH (AC3). Verification: the lint gate (ansible-lint profile min) passes exit 0 on the touched file (V1/AC5); grep for `password` in the edited file returns zero matches (V3). The test gate (ansible-playbook --syntax-check over every playbook) exits 1, but exclusively from four pre-existing failures in unrelated playbooks — role 'docker' not found (create-docker-host.yml), 'instance' is undefined (restart-app.yml, tail-applog.yml), and empty playbook (rollback-container.yml). I confirmed these four errors are identical on the base file state by stashing the edit and re-running the gate: the failure set is unchanged, none reference the edited defaults file, and every playbook that actually loads homelabinfra-defaults.yml (bootstrap.yml, apps, proxmox/create-lxc.yml) syntax-checks clean. The edited defaults file therefore still parses and loads (V2 intent satisfied); the gate's non-zero exit is a pre-existing repository condition outside this change's blast radius, not a regression from this edit.
